locus: Theses in quibus exponitur Doctrina Scholae Romanae circa partitionem Gratiae in sufficientem atque efficacem, & concordiam libertatis humanae cum Gratiae efficacia, XC-CVII (Molina, Concordia question 14, article 13, disputations 40 and 45: with equal aids one converted and another not holds of prevenient grace as prevenient, not of cooperating grace, though the two are really one; conversion not by freedom alone; able not to convert in the composite sense under prevenient grace, only in the divided sense under cooperating grace; grace placed in an illumination of the mind (acquired notions helped by God's influence) and in natural, non-free affections of the will made supernatural by a special influence; the motion that precedes volition (Lucifer, Eve; Isaiah 14:12-14, Genesis 3:6), hindered by the will only indirectly; the motion of uplift toward hope; grace only perfects nature; prevenient motions as vital but not free operations; Molina's own account of the motions toward faith, hope, love and contrition, the infused habits and the last disposition to sanctifying grace; the aid of prevenient grace distinguished from prevenient grace itself).
